title: UAV-BASED WATER RESOURCE MONITORING AT MILITARY FACILITIES: DESIGN AND TECHNOLOGICAL DEVELOPMENT

ABSTRACT

This paper addresses the problem of developing and improving innovative unmanned aerial system (UAS) designs adapted to high-reliability requirements for water resource monitoring at military facilities. The aim of the study is to develop a modular and fault-tolerant UAS architecture with a reliability level of not less than 0,999 based on the technological infrastructure of a higher education institution and to substantiate it through modeling and experimental validation. System reliability is evaluated using a state-space model and the Monte Carlo method. The proposed architecture implements structural redundancy of the control, navigation, communication, and power subsystems. The results show that, compared to non-redundant configurations, the proposed solution provides significantly higher operational robustness and fault tolerance. Experimental tests confirm stable data transmission in the range of 5-20 Mbps, spatial resolution at the level of 5-10 cm/pixel, and flight endurance of 25-35 minutes. The obtained results demonstrate that the developed unmanned aerial system is suitable for reliable and efficient water resource monitoring at military facilities. This work was carried out within the framework of the “BR 249005/0224 Development of innovative designs for the manufacturing and improvement of unmanned aerial systems for special purposes based on the technological infrastructure of higher military educational institutions” funding program.
